purpose: Lexical examples explicitly shown in Richard Ishida's Khmer orthography notes under REAHMUK and coda-diacritic explanations. The source forms and source pronunciation notation are preserved without conversion into project IPA. These are source-attested examples, not independently adjudicated gold items.
transcription_policy: Preserve the source's displayed pronunciation/transliteration string verbatim. It may mix IPA-like symbols with the page's practical transliteration conventions; do not treat it as normalized project IPA.

examples.source_description: REAHMUK after an inherent vowel in an a-class syllable; source describes the rhyme as ah.
REAHMUK after a second-series inherent vowel or AA-sign context; source describes the rhyme as eə̆h.
Short vowel sign I + REAHMUK; the source describes h after the short vowel.
Short vowel sign Y + REAHMUK; source gives this as an example of h after the short vowel.
Short vowel sign U + REAHMUK; source gives this as an example of h after the short vowel.
E-sign + REAHMUK after a first-series consonant; source describes this combination as eh.
E-sign + REAHMUK after a second-series consonant; source describes this combination as ih.
AE-sign + REAHMUK; source describes this combination as eh in an a-class context.
OE-sign + REAHMUK example; source notes the normal spelling ចង្កឹះ and gives the pronunciation string shown here.
OO-sign + REAHMUK after a first-series consonant; source describes the rhyme as ah.
OO-sign + REAHMUK after a second-series consonant; source gives uə̆h (and elsewhere also mentions uh as a possible value for this class).

limitations: No independent audio or second lexical source has been adjudicated for these entries.
The source transcription strings are retained verbatim and are not guaranteed to use the same conventions as project IPA.
The examples do not establish a deterministic rule for every spelling, dialect, stress condition, or register context.
Do not feed these rows directly to a gold-corpus accuracy metric or promote them to deterministic engine output without adjudication.
